11674-the-torrent-entre-naranjos.creator: Unknown
11674-the-torrent-entre-naranjos.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. little boys who in those days used to be hiding behind the wide portal, waiting for a chance to play with the son of the powerful don Ramón Brull, were now the grown men, the sinewy orchard workers, who had been parading from the station to his house, waving their arms, and shouting _vivas_ for their deputy--Alcira's "favorite son."

arxiv-2010-09657.title: PySBD: Pragmatic Sentence Boundary Disambiguation
arxiv-2010-09657.creator: Nipun Sadvilkar, Mark Neumann
arxiv-2010-09657.description: Abstract In this paper, we present a rule-based sentence boundary disambiguation Python package that works out-of-the-box for 22 languages. We aim to provide a realistic segmenter which can provide logical sentences even when the format and domain of the input text is unknown.

arxiv-2110-13260.title: Color-Kinematics Relation from the Feynman Diagram Perspective
arxiv-2110-13260.creator: C.S. Lam
arxiv-2110-13260.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by C.S. Lam. Feynman diagrams for gluon tree amplitudes are studied in the Feynman gauge and in any number of spacetime dimensions. The color-kinematics combinations Δ = n s − n t − n u \Delta=n_{s}-n_{t}-n_{u} of numerators are explicitly calculated for N = 4 , 5 , 6 N=4,5,6 gluons to see whether the color-kinematics relation Δ = 0 \Delta=0 is satisfied.

arxiv-2302-04119.title: Local Law 144: A Critical Analysis of Regression Metrics
arxiv-2302-04119.creator: Giulio Filippi, Sara Zannone, Airlie Hilliard, Adriano Koshiyama
arxiv-2302-04119.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Giulio Filippi, Sara Zannone, Airlie Hilliard, Adriano Koshiyama. The use of automated decision tools in recruitment has received an increasing amount of attention. In November 2021, the New York City Council passed a legislation (Local Law 144) that mandates bias audits of Automated Employment Decision Tools. From 15th April 2023, companies that use automated tools for hiring or promoting employees are required to have these systems audited by an independent entity.

arxiv-2303-04529.title: Cavitation instabilities in amorphous solids via secondary mechanical perturbations
arxiv-2303-04529.creator: Umang A. Dattani 1,2,a , Rishabh Sharma 3,a , Smarajit Karmakar 3,∗ and Pinaki Chaudhuri 1,2
arxiv-2303-04529.description: Abstract Amorphous solids are known to fail catastrophically and in some situations, nano-scaled cavities are believed to play a significant role in the failure. In a recent work, using numerical simulations, we have shown the correspondence between cavitation under uniform expansion of amorphous solids and the yielding under shear.

arxiv-2401-01884.title: A Rewriting-logic-with-SMT-based Formal Analysis and Parameter Synthesis Framework for Parametric Time Petri Nets Volume: 192 Issue: 3-4
arxiv-2401-01884.creator: Jaime Arias LIPN, CNRS UMR 7030 Université Sorbonne Paris Nord, France jaime.arias@lipn.univ-paris13.fr, Kyungmin Bae Pohang University of Science and Technology South Korea kmbae@postech.ac.kr, Carlos Olarte LIPN, CNRS UMR 7030 Université Sorbonne Paris Nord, France carlos.olarte@lipn.univ-paris13.
arxiv-2401-01884.description: Abstract This paper presents a concrete and a symbolic rewriting logic semantics for parametric time Petri nets with inhibitor arcs (PITPNs), a flexible model of timed systems where parameters are allowed in firing bounds. We prove that our semantics is bisimilar to the “standard” semantics of PITPNs.

arxiv-2402-07841.title: Do Membership Inference Attacks Work on Large Language Models?
arxiv-2402-07841.creator: Michael Duan, Anshuman Suri, Niloofar Mireshghallah, Sewon Min, Weijia Shi, Luke Zettlemoyer, Yulia Tsvetkov, Yejin Choi, David Evans, Hannaneh Hajishirzi
arxiv-2402-07841.description: Abstract Membership inference attacks (MIAs) attempt to predict whether a particular datapoint is a member of a target model’s training data. Despite extensive research on traditional machine learning models, there has been limited work studying MIA on the pre-training data of large language models (LLMs).

arxiv-2411-04149.title: Matrix Product States in Quantum Spin Chains
arxiv-2411-04149.description: Abstract In this work, we present a novel representation of matrix product states (MPS) within the framework of quasi-local algebras. By introducing an enhanced compatibility condition, we enable the extension of finite MPS to an infinite-volume state, providing new insights into complex, high-dimensional quantum systems. As an illustrative example, we apply this method to the Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) state.

arxiv-2506-11670.description: Abstract . A new conjecture on characters of finite groups, related to the McKay conjecture, was proposed recently by the first and third authors. In this paper, we prove it for p p -solvable groups when p p is odd. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 20C15 1.

arxiv-2510-04417.title: Partial Information Decomposition via Normalizing Flows in Latent Gaussian Distributions
arxiv-2510-04417.creator: Wenyuan Zhao, Adithya Balachandran, Chao Tian, Paul Pu Liang
arxiv-2510-04417.description: Abstract The study of multimodality has garnered significant interest in fields where the analysis of interactions among multiple information sources can enhance predictive modeling, data fusion, and interpretability. Partial information decomposition (PID) has emerged as a useful information-theoretic framework to quantify the degree to which individual modalities independently, redundantly, or synergistically convey information about a target variable.

arxiv-2510-05685.title: Sample complexity for entropic optimal transport with radial cost
arxiv-2510-05685.creator: Ruiyu Han, Johannes Wiesel
arxiv-2510-05685.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ruiyu Han, Johannes Wiesel. We prove a new sample complexity result for entropy regularized optimal transport. Our bound holds for probability measures on ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} with exponential tail decay and for radial cost functions that satisfy a local Lipschitz condition. It is sharp up to logarithmic factors, and captures the intrinsic dimension of the marginal distributions through a generalized covering number of their supports.

plos-pone-0004587.description: PLOS ONE research article. Previous studies have implicated several brain areas as subserving numerical approximation. Most studies have examined brain correlates of adult numerical approximation and have not considered individual differences in mathematical ability. The present study examined non-symbolic

pmc-10568771.title: Anti-inflammatory and Antiphytopathogenic Fungal Activity of 2,3-seco-Tirucallane Triterpenoids Meliadubins A and B from Melia dubia Cav. Barks with ChemGPS-NP and In Silico Prediction
pmc-10568771.creator: Hieu Tran Trung, Kartiko Arif Purnomo, Szu-Yin Yu, Zih-Jie Yang, Hao-Chun Hu, Tsong-Long Hwang, Nguyen Ngoc Tuan, Le Ngoc Tu, Dau Xuan Duc, Le Dang Quang, Anders Backlund, Tran Dinh Thang, Fang-Rong Chang

Compound 2 exhibited a significant inflammatory inhibition effect toward superoxide anion generation in human neutrophils (EC50 at 5.54 ± 0.36 μM).

pmc-10649102.title: CT Imaging Assessment of Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma Resectability after Neoadjuvant Therapy: Current Status and Perspective on the Use of Radiomics
pmc-10649102.creator: Hala Khasawneh, Hanna Rafaela Ferreira Dalla Pria, Joao Miranda, Rachel Nevin, Shalini Chhabra, Dina Hamdan, Jayasree Chakraborty, Tiago Biachi de Castria, Natally Horvat, Stanley W Ashley
pmc-10649102.description: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is the most common pancreatic cancer and is associated with poor prognosis, a high mortality rate, and a substantial number of healthy life years lost. Surgical resection is the primary treatment option for patients with resectable disease; however, only 10–20% of all patients with PDAC are eligible for resection at the time of diagnosis.

pmc-11456545.title: A “love match” score to compare root exudate attraction and feeding of the plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria Bacillus subtilis, Pseudomonas fluorescens, and Azospirillum brasilense
pmc-11456545.creator: Eulalie Fourneau, Mélissa Pannier, Wassila Riah, Emmanuelle Personeni, Annette Morvan-Bertrand, Josselin Bodilis, Barbara Pawlak
pmc-11456545.description: IntroductionThe rhizosphere is the zone of soil surrounding plant roots that is directly influenced by root exudates released by the plant, which select soil microorganisms. The resulting rhizosphere microbiota plays a key role in plant health and development by enhancing its nutrition or immune response and protecting it from biotic or abiotic stresses.

pmc-11714494.title: Assessing the Influence of Modifiable and Non‐modifiable risk factors on Cognitive and Biomarker Trajectories in Preclinical Alzheimer's Disease: Establishing a Longitudinal Model for Brain Health
pmc-11714494.creator: Luciana Maffei
pmc-11714494.description: BackgroundThe pathogenesis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) begins 15‐20 years before the onset of clinical symptoms, often referred to as the preclinical stage of AD. It is crucial to understand why some individuals develop AD and although biological, psychological, and social factors have been established, their influence in the very early stages of disease trajectories is somewhat unclear.

pmc-12547503.title: Pseudolaric acid B induces G2/M phase arrest in canine mammary tumor cells by targeting CDK1
pmc-12547503.creator: Mengjuan Chen, Hui Han, Mengke Qin, Huixin Li, Qiqi Lu, Xin Huang, Qingda Meng, Shanshan Xie
pmc-12547503.description: IntroductionCurrent management of canine mammary tumors (CMTs) remains reliant on surgical resection and chemotherapy. However, these strategies are often limited by high recurrence rates and systemic toxicity. Addressing these limitations requires urgent development of safer and more effective therapeutics. Pseudolaric acid B (PAB), a bioactive compound extracted from the roots of the Pseudolarix kaempferi Gord.

pmc-12690829.title: The violence of reproductive injustice: Reflections on birth control and its medical epistemics
pmc-12690829.creator: Jana Niemann, Lisa Glaum, Dennis Jepsen, Lea Hofmann, Liane Schenk, Amand Führer
pmc-12690829.description: BackgroundThe widespread promotion of oral contraceptives raises concerns about side effects, informed choices, and contraceptive coercion, which contribute to gynecological violence influenced by systemic factors. The link between gynecological violence and oral contraceptives is understudied and rarely examined through systemic violence theories.

pmc-12786902.title: Hump Nose and Coexisting Deviation in Rhinoplasty: Their Association and Surgical Considerations
pmc-12786902.creator: Su Jin Kim, Je Ho Bang, Kun Hee Lee
pmc-12786902.description: Background/Objectives: Dorsal humps and nasal deviation are common deformities in rhinoplasty. While existing classification systems characterize these deformities individually, their concurrent presentation complicates surgical planning. The aim of this study was to examine the association between dorsal humps and nasal deviation in rhinoplasty patients and assess their influence on surgical decision-making.

pmc-13147124.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A696 MULTIPLEX PROTEOMIC BIOMARKERS FOR ACUTE STROKE SUBTYPE DIFFERENTIATION: AN EXPLORATORY STUDY
pmc-13147124.creator: Julien Paul, Catherine Brassard, Ralph Nuhay, David Chiasson-Ricard, Gloria Ortega-Delgado, Nathalie Arbour, Laura Gioia
pmc-13147124.description: Background and aimsRapid acute stroke triage remains challenging, particularly for early identification of intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and large-vessel-occlusion acute ischemic stroke (LVO-AIS). We assessed whether multiplex proteomics can identify biomarker signatures to improve early stroke subtype classification.MethodsExploratory analyses of a prospective cohort of suspected stroke participants presenting <24 hours from onset.

pmc-13257230.title: QuEChERS-Based LC-MS/MS and HRMS Methods for PFAS Determination in Food: A Systematic Review
pmc-13257230.creator: Francesco Giuseppe Galluzzo, Gaetano Cammilleri, Licia Pantano, Vittorio Calabrese, Maria Drussilla Buscemi, Elisa Maria Domenica Messina, Calogero Alfano, Dario Bonomo, Andrea Pulvirenti, Andrea Macaluso, Vincenzo Ferrantelli, Gianluigi Maria Lo Dico
pmc-13257230.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent contaminants that require very strict performance criteria from the methods that want to analyze them in food for research or regulatory purposes. This systematic literature review tried to evaluate Quick, Easy, Cheap, Effective, Rugged, Safe (QuEChERS) extraction methodologies coupled with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) and high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) for PFAS determination in food.

pmc-13314913.title: Optimizing Subcutaneous Antibody Dosing Regimens Through Operating Space Maps: rHuPH20 Case Study
pmc-13314913.creator: Ryan P Nolan, Harish Chintakuntla
pmc-13314913.description: Therapeutic antibody dosing regimens are often constrained by formulation and administration factors that limit flexibility in dose and schedule. Subcutaneous (SC) delivery offers advantages over intravenous (IV) administration—such as improved convenience and potentially more favorable pharmacokinetic (PK) profiles—but is typically restricted by injection volume, requiring lower doses and more frequent dosing.

pmc-13363195.title: Prevalence and competing risk of psychiatric comorbidities in chronic low back pain by age group
pmc-13363195.creator: Ryan J. Pontiff, Abigail Helm, Sadaf Arefi Milani, Melissa Morrow, Carole A. Tucker
pmc-13363195.description: Patients with nonspecific chronic low back pain increasingly develop anxiety, depression, insomnia, and substance use disorders, with patterns varying by age and sex requiring tailored screening. 1. Introduction Chronic pain, defined as persistent or recurrent discomfort lasting beyond 3 months, affects approximately 24% of US adults and represents one of the most significant public health challenges in modern health care.

pmc-13554656.title: Barriers and Facilitators in Access to Care Among Adults With Traumatic Spinal Cord Injuries: A Qualitative Study Comparing VA and Commercial Insurance
pmc-13554656.creator: Analay Perez, Tyler G James, Elham Mahmoudi
pmc-13554656.description: BackgroundIndividuals with traumatic spinal cord injuries (TSCI) can encounter different experiences when accessing care, especially between individuals receiving care from the Veterans Affair (VA) health care insurance and commercial insurance.ObjectivesThe purpose of this study was to explore the barriers and facilitators in access to care among individuals with TSCI receiving care from the VA and commercial insurance.

pmc-13559130.title: Ultrasound-based nomogram for predicting high-risk hepatic portal venous gas in children: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13559130.creator: Chao Ma, Pengling Huang, Guanghua Pei, Zhaowei Meng

pmc-13609574.title: Platelet-Rich Plasma in Recurrent Pregnancy Loss: Toward a Precision Medicine Framework for Biologically Guided Patient Selection
pmc-13609574.creator: Sofoklis Stavros, Anastasios Potiris, Maria Anastasia Daskalaki, Stefanos Dafopoulos, Efthalia Moustakli, Theodoros Karampitsakos, Dimos Sioutis, Konstantinos Dafopoulos, Nikolaos Thomakos, George Daskalakis, Peter Drakakis
pmc-13609574.description: Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL), a multifactorial condition in reproductive medicine, affects approximately 1–3% of couples. Increasing evidence implicates endometrial dysfunction, immune dysregulation, impaired angiogenesis, and oxidative stress (OS) in its pathophysiology, highlighting the need for biologically targeted therapeutic strategies. In this context, platelet-rich plasma (PRP) has emerged as a regenerative approach with the potential to modulate these underlying mechanisms.
